context.situation: I chair the regional fisheries authority. Our scientific advisers recommend a 40% cut in the catch limit. Landings have been stable for three years, which the fleet takes as evidence the stock is healthy. The advisers say stable landings can mask decline because the fleet is fishing harder and using better gear on a shrinking area. A 40% cut would put roughly half the small boats out of business within a season, in communities with no other employment. I am minded to take a 10% cut and review in two years.
context.whatMatters: Keeping the fleet viable; not destroying coastal communities.
context.stakeholders: Fleet, coastal communities, scientific advisers, future fishers.
context.uncertainties: Whether stable landings reflect a stable stock.
context.recoveryHorizon: Advisers say stock recovery could take decades if it collapses.

evidence.text: Landings have been stable for three years.
Advisers state stable landings can mask decline under increasing effort.
Fishing effort and gear efficiency have both increased.
The fleet reads stable landings as a healthy stock.
A 40% cut would end roughly half the small boat businesses in one season.
Advisers state recovery from collapse could take decades.
